EICMA 2026 • Here Are Some of the Serious and Obscure Brands That EICMA 2026 Had To Offer – Worth Knowing About
Help Me Pick My Next Car – Spoiler Alert: It’s Not Going To Be Easy!
13 photos
Photo: BMW
If there’s one thing that brings us all together, it is the car virus , this incurable disease that has eaten through our finances ever since we got our first paycheck. Some of us have lost contact with those who we once thought we’d have by our side forever due to our car obsession, and some have simply managed to move on.
What does the latter part mean? Well, in my case, a nice car that relatively reliable, looks good, drives good, and does not tend to bankrupt me in case things go south. On top of that, my ride is comfortable and quiet, because I have reached an age when straight-piping feels like absolute nonsense, and stiff suspensions are definitely a no-no. By the way, been there and done that, as I absolutely loved cars with the suspension travel of a dining table a couple of decades ago.
From a gearhead’s perspective, because this is what this story is all about, I am absolutely disappointed in everything the car industry stands for today. Have you driven modern vehicles? You probably have, and while you can still get a nice and very reliable truck/ SUV /pickup, I am not into high-riders and never were, even if I used to own a crossover from Jeep at one point that I absolutely hated. You can read that story here , by the way, though preferably after you are done with this one.
I don’t have a numerous family, so station wagons are out of the question, though to be honest, I wouldn’t mind a nice C8 Audi RS 6 Avant. I could probably get one with a stretch, but then again, that wouldn’t be a financially-wise decision. Coupe and convertibles are not exactly my thing either, unless we are talking about a luxury-oriented fixed-roof model. You know, something like a C217 Mercedes S-Class Coupe.
Photo: BMW Then again, buying one of those would again not be a wise decision, as not only they’re not the most reliable out there, but they are also quite plasticky. And I absolutely hate car crickets. Therefore, sedans are definitely my cup of tea. And while I’m at it, these would need to check numerous boxes in order to be appealing to me. Comfort it a must, good looks, too, and pretty much everything I already mentioned a few paragraphs above.
If you’ve been following my stories, then you know that I am fond of two car manufacturers: BMW and Lamborghini. And while the latter is out of reach, for now anyway, not to mention that their rides are not exactly great daily drivers, nor to they go easy on the wallet. And no, Lambos do not mean the Urus. That’s a rebodied Volkswagen Touareg with numerous other mods, and while I can understand the fact that it’s a huge moneymaker for the Raging Bull, I would never buy one , regardless of how much money I have in the bank.
Thus, it’s pretty much all about BMWs for me. And they have to be sedans for the above reasons. The 2 Series Coupe is a great driver’s car, and the M2 is absolutely dreamy. But I don’t plan on spending too much money on gasoline, especially since the juice has significantly gone up nowadays. The 3er is an absolute icon, and the M3 is an even bigger one. But I want something bigger and a lot more comfortable.
The 7 Series seems pointless to me, as it’s simply too big and heavy, and therefore, I settled for the 5 Series. In fact, I’m currently at the third 5er, and all of them have been F10s by choice. I didn’t get to enjoy my first due to a reason called divorce. The second one was very Spartan, though it did go extremely easy on my wallet during some challenging times for me, and when those times ended, I sold it and bought my third F10.
Photo: BMW It needed to check to major (for me) boxes: feature an automatic transmission, and most of my driving is urban, and I live in a very crowded city, and have a sunroof, because I love to look at the sky above every now and then. And it ended up coming with much more equipment. Leather upholstery, power-adjustable seats, a Bang & Olufsen (not Harman Kardon, by the way) premium sound system, ambient lighting, a head-up display, xDrive AWD, adjustable suspension, and so on.
I’m now in my third year of owning this F10 BMW 5 Series LCI , and while it is still a great machine in my opinion, I am now starting to search for my next one on the used car market. I’d like a newer one, but the G60 is not my cup of tea. I find it ugly both inside and out, and the facelifted iteration that’s in the making as we speak will enter the Neue Klasse era, so it would feel more like a downgrade rather than an upgrade.
The G30 does not look that good compared to the F10, at least on the outside, so what should I get? I Don’t like the new Audi A6, the modern-day Mercedes E-Class is too much of a screen fest. Jaguar is now on the white stuff, I don’t fancy Lexus’ and Infiniti’s rides. In my eyes, Volvo is a Europe-based Chinese marque at this point (ahem, Geely), and don’t even get me started on EVs. You could say the Porsche Panamera, but it’s not exactly a looker, is it? On top of that, the maintenance would be challenging to say the least.
Unless I am missing something (Cadillac, erm, nope!), that pretty much sums up this class. I don’t want a mainstream car from Mazda, Toyota, and so on, even if there is no major difference anymore between these things and premium ones, especially if you aim for a top grade. So, what am I left with? Probably my current Bimmer , which would be a lot nicer with a nicer set of wheels and a new timing chain. So, I’d better keep writing, as the latter is a must next year.
